newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Romania has obtained Spain's support for its bid to join NATO in a first wave of the alliance's expansion, Senate chairman Petre Roman told a news conference after his visit to Spain.
He said that Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes had openly and clearly expressed his country's intention to back Romania's bid for quick NATO admission.
* Romania's former King Michael left Romania, ending a six-day visit after his Romanian citizenship was restored.
Michael pledged to make all efforts to promote Romania abroad and help its European and NATO integration aspirations.
* Romanian authorities should have greeted King Michael at the highest protocol level and not as an "ordinary citizen", National Liberal Party PNL-CD leader Niculae Cerveni told a news conference.

* Opposition National Unity Party (PUNR) will back a motion introduced by the leftist opposition Party of Social Democracy against the government's farming policy, a PUNR official said. He said PUNR believes the current crisis in agriculture requires debates and urgent measures.
* PUNR will never agree with the signature of the Romanian- Ukrainian treaty as long as it allows that Romania be stripped of some of its historical territories, the PUNR offical said.

* Senate's legal commission rejected the justice minister's request to strip Senator Vadim Tudor of his parliamentary immunity, over slander allegations following stories published in his weekly "Romania Mare".
Tudor said he hoped the Senate's decision would coincide with that of the commission.

* Romania's chances to gain quick NATO admission have substantially increased recently, Karl Heinz Hornhus, head of the German Bundestag's foreign policy commission, told a news conference in Bucharest. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
